_comment: C5-PROJ-A source capability / access / lineage census. Governed by docs/PROJECTION_ENSEMBLE_PLAN_2026-08-15.md. This records WHAT EXISTS TODAY and WHAT IS AUTHORIZED, not a plan to build. It authorizes no automation by itself — see accessPosture per entry. Narrative record: docs/projections/C5_PROJ_A_SOURCE_CAPABILITY_CENSUS.md. Loader/validator: src/ros/projection_source_census.py.

evidenceClassNotes.PROJECTION_MODEL: A real per-player projected stat line or fantasy-point projection from a season-long fantasy model.
evidenceClassNotes.DFS_PROJECTION: A daily-fantasy projection, distinguished from salary/ownership/optimizer output or rankings.
evidenceClassNotes.BETTING_MARKET: A sportsbook player-prop line + price, de-vigged before use — never an independent projection-model vote.
evidenceClassNotes.RANKINGS_ONLY: Not one of the plan's three evidence classes. An ordinal ranking, ECR or ADP board with no per-player projected stat line or point total behind it. C5-PROJ-A's own brief requires flagging these explicitly rather than silently admitting them as projections.

accessPostureNotes.KEYED_API_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED: A documented commercial API that requires a per-account key. Permission is a licensing question (licensingStatus); the KEY is an operational question: it lives only in the named environment variable (credentialEnvVar), never in the repo, a log or an exception. An absent key makes the source UNAVAILABLE (fetch answers credential_missing) — never zero data, and never a blocker for any other source. Activation is flag ON + key present + last fetch healthy (the module's source_available()).
accessPostureNotes.PUBLIC_UNDOCUMENTED_NO_AUTH: A specific endpoint is recorded and answers without any credential, but it is not part of the provider's documented/published API and no artifact in this repo records terms permitting automated consumption or internal redistribution. Reachable is not licensed. Fails closed — does not authorize production automation; the owning feature flag stays OFF until the licensing open item is resolved.
accessPostureNotes.PUBLIC_NO_AUTH: No login or credential needed; automation is a straightforward fetch.
accessPostureNotes.CREDENTIALED_SESSION_ALREADY_WIRED: A working authenticated session already exists in this repo for a DIFFERENT product from the same vendor (typically dynasty rankings). Reusing it for a projection endpoint is a session-scope question, not a new credential question.
accessPostureNotes.SUBSCRIPTION_SCOPE_UNRECORDED: The owner reports subscription/account access, but no artifact in this repo records that the subscription's terms permit automated acquisition and internal redistribution of the specific data. Per the governing plan §3: 'Subscription access must not be silently equated with unrestricted automated acquisition/redistribution rights.' Fails closed — does not authorize production automation.
accessPostureNotes.NO_ACCESS_PATH_RECORDED: Owner reports general permission/access is plausible, but no specific authorized endpoint, login, or terms have been recorded. Fails closed.

sources.notes: IMPORTANT DISCREPANCY, recorded rather than silently carried forward: src/ros/sources/__init__.py's ROS_SOURCES registry marks draftSharksRosSf as is_projection_source: True (see the sibling entry below) while its own module docstring says it currently reads a dynasty RANKINGS CSV as a proxy. sources.displayName: Sleeper weekly projections (RotoWire stat lines served by Sleeper)

modelAncestry.evidence: Every row of a full 2026 week-3 capture taken 2026-09-25T00:58Z (7,630 of 7,630; a trimmed 18-row sample is committed at tests/fixtures/game_day/sleeper_projections/) carries company: "rotowire". The independence family is therefore RotoWire, not Sleeper: a separately ingested RotoWire product, or a consensus containing RotoWire (e.g. Yahoo's), is the SAME family and must not vote twice. The parser checks the per-row company field and refuses rows naming any other model rather than relabelling them.

sources.accessEvidence: https://api.sleeper.app/projections/nfl/<season>/<week>?season_type=regular&position[]=... answers without authentication. It is NOT under Sleeper's documented public API root (api.sleeper.app/v1, which this repo already uses for leagues/rosters/matchups); it is the endpoint Sleeper's own web client calls.
sources.licensingOpenItem: No artifact records that Sleeper's or RotoWire's terms permit automated consumption or internal redistribution of these projections. The RotoWire model is a commercial product surfaced through Sleeper. OPEN ITEM for an owner decision — the feature flag stays OFF until it is resolved. Do not treat reachability as clearance.
sources.notes: C5-PROJ-C first WEEKLY source. Seasonal intelligence lane ONLY: weekly per-player projected stat lines, rescored under the caller's exact league card by src.league_intel.scorer.score_stat_line — never a dynasty value, rank or vote. Rows with no projection (Sleeper ships a placeholder carrying only adp_dd_ppr, no game_id) are reported as missing, never as a 0-point projection. Threshold/bonus and special-teams categories the provider does not publish are reported per player as uncovered, never silently zero.

sources.displayName: Fantasy Nerds weekly projections (Nerd Rank consensus, offense + IDP)

modelAncestry.evidence: Fantasy Nerds describes its projections as a consensus: it aggregates 'rankings and projections from a number of sites around the net' and weights each by measured accuracy (Nerd Rank). Constituent list from https://www.fantasynerds.com/about/nerd-rank; consensus-projection statement on https://www.fantasynerds.com/nfl/weekly-projections (both retrieved 2026-09-25). Which constituents feed the WEEKLY PROJECTION consensus specifically (vs the rankings) is not published, so every named constituent is treated as a possible ancestor — conservative: a possible correlation is declared rather than assumed away. constituentFamilies maps the constituents onto census family names (rotowire = the sleeperWeeklyProjections family; espnClay = ESPN's projections are Mike Clay's). An ensemble must not count this source AND any source whose family is in constituentFamilies as independent votes (src.ros.projection_source_census.ancestry_overlaps).

sources.accessEvidence: Documented API https://api.fantasynerds.com/docs/nfl: GET https://api.fantasynerds.com/v1/nfl/weekly-projections?apikey=<key> ('Weeks 1 - 18') and GET https://api.fantasynerds.com/v1/nfl/idp-weekly?apikey=<key>. The key is a query parameter only; the module keeps it out of every stored URL, log and error. No week parameter is documented (the feed serves the provider's current week).
sources.responseSchemaNote: The docs publish no response field names or sample body. The stat mapping is keyed on the categories shown on the public weekly page (QB CMP/ATT/PASS YDS/PASS TD/INT/RUSH YDS/RUSH TD/FMBL; RB/WR/TE REC/REC YDS/REC TD/RUSH ATT; K XP/FG; IDP TKLS/ASS TKLS/SACKS/PASS DEF/INT) with explicit accepted spellings; ambiguous categories (FMBL, bare TKLS, bare XP/FG) are deliberately unmapped. A mismatch fails the fetch health check (no_mapped_stats + unmapped_provider_fields), so the source cannot become available on an unrecognised schema. The first credentialed capture is the schema check: commit it (key stripped) as a fixture, extend STAT_MAPPING to the real field names, and set SCHEMA_VERIFIED.
sources.notes: Seasonal intelligence lane ONLY — never a dynasty value, rank or vote. Coverage from the public categories: no targets, first downs, returns/special teams, kicker distance bands or misses, or IDP TFL/QB hit/FF/FR/TD — each league-paid key of those kinds is reported per player as uncovered, never zero. Identity: Fantasy Nerds' own playerId; the caller injects the identity-owner resolver (unresolved rows refused and listed).

sources.displayName: SportsDataIO projected player game stats by week (offense + IDP feed)

modelAncestry.evidence: SportsDataIO describes its projections as 'proprietary in-house machine learning models' ('a data-driven model using historical match ups and statistics'), customized per game by Tuesday 2 pm ET and 'updated every 15 minutes until kick off' (https://sportsdata.io/developers/workflow-guide/nfl, retrieved 2026-09-25). Its own family. FantasyData is the same company/model: a FantasyData-branded projection feed would be the SAME family, not a second vote.

sources.accessEvidence: NFL v3 Projections API (OpenAPI description https://api.apis.guru/v2/specs/sportsdata.io/nfl-v3-projections/1.0/openapi.json; portal https://sportsdata.io/developers/api-documentation/nfl): GET https://api.sportsdata.io/v3/nfl/projections/json/PlayerGameProjectionStatsByWeek/{season}{REG|PRE|POST}/{week} and .../IdpPlayerGameProjectionStatsByWeek/{season}REG/{week}. The key is sent in the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header (the documented alternative to the ?key= query parameter), so it never appears in a URL. The IDP feed may be a separate subscription scope; its failure does not affect the offense feed.
sources.notes: Seasonal intelligence lane ONLY — never a dynasty value, rank or vote. Stat lines mapped field-by-field to Sleeper stat keys (src/ros/sportsdataio_weekly_projections.py::STAT_MAPPING) and rescored under the caller's exact card. Kicker: made by distance band, attempts and PATs (fgmiss/xpmiss derived linearly); NOT covered: made-FG total distance (fgm_yds) and misses by distance band. IDP: solo/assisted/total tackles, sacks, sack yards, TFL, QB hits, PD, FF, FR, INT, return yards, TDs, safeties, blocks. NOT covered: first downs, reception-length buckets, *_40p play bonuses, yardage/tackle thresholds (never derived from a projected mean). The published schema has no per-row update stamp; the payload Last-Modified header is used when sent, else ensemble dating refuses (fetch time is not data freshness). Identity: SportsDataIO PlayerID = Sleeper fantasy_data_id; the caller injects the identity-owner resolver.

sources.accessEvidence: N/A — internal model, no external access question.
